region.name: Board And Investor Updates
region.summary: Drafts, talking points, and metrics snapshots for 2026 board meetings and investor updates, covering the Northfield Series B term sheet, burn and runway, Investing GA, the Sep 26 incident, ACH cut-over, SOC 2, and VP Eng hiring.

brief.text:
This region holds the working materials behind the company's 2026 board meetings and investor communications, all oriented toward closing the Series B. The anchor fact is the Northfield Ventures term sheet: $38M at a $210M post-money valuation, with close targeted around Nov 14. Existing investors (Granite Peak and angels) are getting a September investor update email covering the term sheet, end-of-September metrics, Investing beta and GA go/no-go dates, the Sep 26 double-debit incident and its remediation, ACH pipeline stability, card issuing slipping to Q1 2027, team size, and hiring asks. That draft is waiting on an open, high-priority Aleks edit pass with send deadlines attached. Two questions in it are still unresolved: whether to disclose the Sep 26 incident, and whether to name VP Eng candidates. Earlier board-update inputs record a decision to report the ACH cut-over slip honestly. They also log 14 investor first meetings, Hollis Partners engaged for the VP Eng search, Nadia on a manager-track trial, and engineering hires since May.

The end-of-September metrics snapshot, confirmed with Jordan on 10/3, is the source of truth for the data room, the October board deck, and the investor update. It shows MAU, MTU, subscription ARR, burn, and runway against the May baseline, and it warns not to mix pre-close and post-close runway figures. Supporting September numbers: headcount is 64, with 31 in engineering. There were zero missed NACHA cutoffs and one SEV1 (Sep 26). The snapshot also records KYC migration savings and burn rising about $60k/month against $1.2M of ARR growth. The August board update inputs still carried TK placeholders for user and revenue numbers owned by Jordan and Kavi, along with status on the ACH cut-over, KYC migration, Investing, and SOC 2.

The Oct 21 board meeting talking points cover the scorecard, the Investing GA decision, ownership of the Sep 26 incident, the VP Eng hire, the 55% offer-accept rate, the SOC 2 Type II exception, and asks for payments-engineer intros. The tracked risks map onto those points. The most severe is Investing GA being held for position reconciliation and Android parity (severity 18). Lower-severity open risks are the legacy system lacking a safeguard against double debits (the root of Sep 26), position reconciliation errors after corporate actions, and the 55% offer-accept rate, which the user owns. Typical questions this region answers include what the Series B terms and close date are, which metrics figures are authoritative, what burn and runway look like, whether and how to disclose the Sep 26 incident, why Investing GA is gated, the status of SOC 2 and card issuing, and what remains before the investor update can go out.

items.summary: Card issuing is deferred to Q1 2027 to focus on investing GA and the round.

items.title: Decision: Investing beta conditions
items.summary: Pillar signed off on Aug 28 with a $2,500/user daily funding cap for the first 90 days. Beta planned for Sep 8 at 5% of MTU.

items.title: Open Question: Mention Sep 26 incident in investor email?
items.summary: Aleks is unsure; the author wants it included since investors would hear it via Northfield's diligence otherwise, and the board meeting is Oct 21.

items.title: Open Question: Whether to name VP Eng candidates
items.summary: Notes lean toward no VP Eng names in the email, but the decision is explicitly not yet made.
